article.title: Omisión de を en conversación informal
article.part: Partículas y relaciones — 助詞と関係
article.chapter: Objeto y partículas centrales: を/に/で/へ — 目的語と主要助詞：を／に／で／へ

claims.summary: Fujii and Ono (2000) study occurrence and non-occurrence of the Japanese direct-object marker o in spontaneous informal conversation; their abstract characterizes zero marking as the unmarked option for direct objects.

claims.sectionKey: Cuándo aparece を en el estudio
claims.summary: The study abstract says overt o is used when the direct-object NP information is salient in discourse or cognitive processing requires additional effort, describing object marking as a device for selective focus.
The entry confines its claim to the authors’ reported study on spontaneous informal conversation and does not infer universal omission across registers or reproduce unverified sample utterances.
